blocks.text: Modalities are mostly **adjuncts**. They may reduce pain or swelling in the short term, but rarely change long-term outcomes alone. Choose them when they support active treatment, and explain their limited role honestly.

sections.title: C. Decision checklist before using a modality

items: Is there a clear objective (for example reduce pain enough to start exercise)?
Is there evidence for this condition?
Could the patient do this themselves at home (heat, ice, TENS) to save clinic time for active care?
How will you measure whether it helped?

blocks.label: TEACHER'S VOICE
body: If you would remove a modality and the treatment plan would work just as well, the modality was not adding value. Spend that time on education and exercise.

items: **Name one contraindication for TENS.** Over the anterior neck (also pacemaker without advice, abdomen in pregnancy).
**Which modality has support for persistent plantar heel pain?** Extracorporeal shockwave therapy.
**Is therapeutic ultrasound routinely recommended for back pain?** No.
**What is NMES useful for after knee surgery?** Improving quadriceps activation.
**Why prefer home-based heat or TENS?** Saves clinic time for active treatment and supports self-management.
